spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: ## Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: PS nanospheres with core–shell structure were synthesized by the one-step emulsion polymerization method.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: Briefly, styrene (38.0 g), acrylic acid (2.0 g) and methyl methacrylate (2.0 g) were dispersed in 160 ml of water.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: 0–0.011 mmol emulsifier sodium dodecyl benzene sulfonate (lower than the critical micelle concentration) and 12.50 mmol of buffer agent of ammonium bicarbonate was dissolved previously.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: The reaction mixture was kept at 70 °C for 0.5 h.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: Aqueous solution of APS as the initiator was added separately three times (24 ml, 8 ml, 8 ml of 4.25 mmol) and stirring was maintained at 80 °C for 1.5 h.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: Then the temperature was increased to 80 °C before the second addition of APS and was reacted for another 2 h.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: Finally, the polymerization reaction was carried out at 80 °C for 2 h with continuous stirring for the third addition of APS solution.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: The resulting particles were centrifuged (taking the supernatant, 8,000 rpm, 20 min) several times to wash away the excess polymer.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: Formulating stabilized and dispersed colloidal nanoparticle ink

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: The colloidal particle supernatant was first concentrated by high-speed centrifugation (12,000 rpm, 20 min) and then dispersed in the solvent of formamide by ultrasonication (40 Hz, 30 min).

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: The mass concentrations of the colloidal nanoparticles, ranging from 0.5 to 40 wt%, were adjusted by controlling the added solvent mass.

spans.heading: Preparing monodispersed core-shell PS nanoparticles
spans.text: The nanoparticle ink exhibits suitable printing parameters (such as viscosity: 3.84 mPa s, surface tension: 57.31 mN m $^{-1}$ , boiling point: 210 °C).

spans.heading: Fabricating hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrates
spans.text: ## Fabricating hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrates

spans.heading: Fabricating hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrates
spans.text: The substrates with smooth surface were sequentially sonicated in methanol, acetone and deionized water for 15 min and then blow-dried with nitrogen.

spans.heading: Fabricating hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrates
spans.text: To increase the surface energy, the substrates were treated with air plasma (DT02S, OPS Plasma Technology Co., Ltd.) at 200 W for 200 s.

spans.heading: Fabricating hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrates
spans.text: Then the superhydrophilic substrates were surface-modified with different molecules, such as the 1H,1H,2H, 2H-perfluorodecyltrimethoxysilane, (3-glycidoxypropyl)trimethoxysilane and triethoxy-n-octylsilane by chemical vapour deposition at 80 °C for 3 h.

spans.heading: Fabricating hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrates
spans.text: Finally, the modified hydrophobic substrates were immersed in ethanol for 2 h, blow-dried with nitrogen to remove the physically deposited molecules and stored in Petri dishes.

spans.heading: Fabricating heterogeneous wettability substrates
spans.text: ## Fabricating heterogeneous wettability substrates

spans.heading: Fabricating heterogeneous wettability substrates
spans.text: The preparation process of heterogeneous wettability consists of the following steps.

spans.heading: Fabricating heterogeneous wettability substrates
spans.text: First, photolithography is used to prepare the patterned substrates, with the photoresist pattern serving as hydrophilic pins.

spans.heading: Fabricating heterogeneous wettability substrates
spans.text: The substrate is then subjected to an overall hydrophilic treatment, so that the surface of the unpatterned region is grafted with hydrophilic groups.

spans.heading: Fabricating heterogeneous wettability substrates
spans.text: Finally, using the strategy of gas-phase grafting of hydrophobic molecules, the hydrophilic regions can be converted into the hydrophobic regions that are combined with the hydrophilic pins into heterogeneous wettability.

spans.heading: Fabricating black background
spans.text: ## Fabricating black background

spans.heading: Fabricating black background
spans.text: The black background was prepared by doping commercial PDMS with the black dye nigrosine.

spans.heading: Fabricating black background
spans.text: First, the PDMS prepolymer and curing agent were mixed thoroughly and homogenously dispersed at a mass ratio of 10:1.

spans.heading: Fabricating black background
spans.text: Then nigrosine powder (Sigma-Aldrich) was added as the black dye at a mass fraction of 2 wt% relative to the PDMS prepolymer.

spans.heading: Fabricating black background
spans.text: Finally, the well-dispersed mixture was cast onto the back surface of the printed film and cured at 80 °C for 2 h, yielding a smooth, flat and uniform black PDMS background.

spans.heading: Printing DCPCs
spans.text: ## Printing DCPCs

spans.heading: Printing DCPCs
spans.text: The designed pattern was based on the binary bitmap.

spans.heading: Printing DCPCs
spans.text: Controlled by the digital designed pattern, the colloidal ink was printed on the hydrophobic and low-adhesion substrate with the inkjet printing technology (independent R&D and customization) to form the domed microdroplets.

spans.heading: Printing DCPCs
spans.text: After printing, the substrate was placed in situ and dried at room temperature (25 °C) to ensure the free movement of three-phase contact line and ordered self-assembly of the colloidal nanoparticles.

spans.heading: Coating PDMS polymer matrix
spans.text: ## Coating PDMS polymer matrix

spans.heading: Coating PDMS polymer matrix
spans.text: Prepolymer of PDMS (SYLGARD 184 silicone elastomer kit, Dow) was prepared by mixing the monomers with the curing agent (with a mass ratio of 10:1) and stirred by a mechanical stirrer for 10 min.

spans.heading: Coating PDMS polymer matrix
spans.text: To remove the air bubbles, the prepolymer was centrifuged (3,000 rpm, 5 min).

spans.heading: Coating PDMS polymer matrix
spans.text: Then the prepolymer was printed on the surface of the nano-assemblies by blade and left for 5 min, allowing the prepolymer to spread and fully penetrate the voids between the nanoparticles.

spans.heading: Coating PDMS polymer matrix
spans.text: The thickness of the PDMS was controlled by adjusting the volume of the prepolymer.

spans.heading: Curing the PDMS prepolymer
spans.text: ## Curing the PDMS prepolymer

spans.heading: Curing the PDMS prepolymer
spans.text: The PDMS prepolymer was continuously irradiated for 10 min by the lamps (Philips, 250 W).

spans.heading: Curing the PDMS prepolymer
spans.text: With the polymerization of PDMS, the nano-assemblies would automatically form a robust composite unit with the polymer network.

spans.heading: Peeling off the cured PDMS
spans.text: ## Peeling off the cured PDMS

spans.heading: Peeling off the cured PDMS
spans.text: The cured PDMS was directly peeled off from the substrate.

spans.heading: Peeling off the cured PDMS
spans.text: As the PDMS was peeled and flipped, the meta-assemblies would be immediately formed.

spans.heading: Peeling off the cured PDMS
spans.text: In the R2R-ANP process, large-scale meta-assembly patterns were rolled up by wheel curling.

spans.heading: Experimental details during R2R processing
spans.text: ## Experimental details during R2R processing

spans.heading: Experimental details during R2R processing
spans.text: Inkjet printing: nozzle diameter (25 $\mu$ m), inter-nozzle spacing (100 $\mu$ m), droplet volume (10 pl), printing speed (2 mm s $^{-1}$ ), jetting frequency (0.5–20.0 Hz), droplet drying temperature (70 °C); PDMS blading: blade gap (0.5 mm), blade height (1.5 mm), blading speed (2 mm s $^{-1}$ ); thermal curing: curing temperature (180 °C), curing time per unit length (5 s cm $^{-1}$ ); peeling: peeling angle (45°), peeling speed (2 mm s $^{-1}$ ), applied pressure (0.1 MPa); rolling: winding tension (5 N), winding speed (synchronized with the printing speed, 3 mm s $^{-1}$ ).

spans.heading: Experimental details during R2R processing
spans.text: To enable high-efficiency R2R printing, the following details should be noted, including: preheating of the set-up to ensure rapid solvent evaporation and PDMS curing; presetting the module speeds to ensure coordination among various processing sections; overall cleanliness of the set-up to prevent optical defects.

spans.heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.semantic_heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.text: ## Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization

spans.heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.semantic_heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.text: Microscale optical intensity measurements were performed using standard bright-field microscopy photography (Nikon ECLIPSE Ti) and image processing.

spans.heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.semantic_heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.text: First, the reflection meta-assembly images were captured under identical illumination conditions and exposure time.

spans.heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.semantic_heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.text: Then the intensity values were quantitatively extracted through image processing and normalized against the maximum and minimum values among the images.

spans.heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.semantic_heading: Microscopic optical intensity test and normalization
spans.text: The maximum reflectance intensity of the tested samples was scaled to 1 as the upper reference and the minimum reflectance intensity was defined as 0 as the lower reference.

spans.heading: Macroscopic optical performance test
spans.text: ## Macroscopic optical performance test

spans.heading: Macroscopic optical performance test
spans.text: Macroscopic images were taken by placing the sample on a black background.

spans.heading: Macroscopic optical performance test
spans.text: Furthermore, the protective layer, such as PDMS, was coated onto the surface of the sample to prevent contaminations.

spans.heading: Macroscopic optical performance test
spans.text: For uniform colouration, the following viewing conditions are recommended: (1) ensure collimated incident light; (2) maintain a sufficiently small distance between the observation point and the light source (typically <2 cm); (3) ensure that the observer maintains a proper distance from the sample; (4) mount the sample on a black substrate to eliminate background reflection, absorb scattered light and enhance colour contrast.

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: ## Mechanical performance test

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: Stretching measurements were conducted by stretching the microscopic meta-assembly pattern using a Stepper Motor Controller (Beijing J&M Technologies Co., Ltd.).

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: The test was conducted under displacement control at a constant rate of $5 \, mm s^{-1}$ with the equivalent path length of 10 mm.

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: Digital cameras were used to record the stretching process.

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: Similarly, the cycles-to-failure behaviours of the meta-assembly were tested at a constant rate of $30 \, mm s^{-1}$ with cycle number of 10,000.

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: During the test, the optical microscopy images were recorded and analysed at the initial, intermediate and final of the cycle test.

spans.heading: Mechanical performance test
spans.text: Other mechanical properties, such as bending and twisting, are verified directly by manual operations and recorded in real time by the digital camera.

spans.heading: Stability tests
spans.text: ## Stability tests

spans.heading: Stability tests
spans.text: Ultraviolet light (365 nm, 400 W) exposure was used to perform the accelerated light ageing tests.

spans.heading: Stability tests
spans.text: Low-temperature tests were performed by placing the sample in the freezer compartment of a commercial refrigerator for 24 h.

spans.heading: Stability tests
spans.text: High-temperature tests were performed by placing the sample on a hotplate with the temperature ranging from 50 to 250 °C for 24 h.

spans.heading: Stability tests
spans.text: Solvent resistance tests were performed by submerging the sample in a range of solvents for 24 h, including pure water, aqueous sodium hydroxide solution (1 mol l $^{-1}$ ), aqueous solution of acetic acid (1 mol l $^{-1}$ ), ethanol and hexadecane.

spans.heading: Stability tests
spans.text: Washing tests were performed by placing the sample into a commercial washing machine with the working time ranging from 10 to 150 min.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: ## Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The finite-difference time-domain simulation technique was performed to understand the near-field coupling between the incident light and meta-assemblies.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The hemispherical meta-assembly was composed of nanospheres that were positioned in a close-packed arrangement.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The meta-assembly was submerged in PDMS-like low-refractive-index media ( $n_{eff} = 1.41$ ).

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The upper layers of the meta-assembly were set as air-like environments ( $n_{eff} = 1$ ).

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: A plane-wave source was placed 5 $\mu$ m above the top of the meta-assembly.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The polarization direction of the incident wave was transverse-magnetic.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: To show the near-field mode profile, a two-dimensional field monitor (x-y plane monitor) was also inserted.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The boundary condition for the z-direction was a standard perfect matched layer to eliminate unwanted reflection.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: Topological polarization was achieved by changing the meta-assembly morphology from a circular shape to quadrilaterals and octagons.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: C was set as the degree of circular polarization and E was set as the intensity of the electric field. $C \times E$ was set as the intensity of the circular polarization component.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: The polarization change was explored by changing the incident polarization angles.

spans.heading: Numerical simulation of meta-assemblies
spans.text: More simulation details are summarized in the Supplementary Materials.

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: ## Characterizations

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: The dispersity of the colloidal nanoparticles was measured by a granulometer (ZetaPALS BI-90Plus, Brookhaven Instruments).

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: Contact angles were measured using a contact angle measurement device (OCA20, DataPhysics) with the polymer droplet (2 $\mu$ l).

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: The printed colloidal assemblies and microcavities were characterized by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (JEOL JSM-7500F) at an accelerating voltage of 5.0 kV.

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: The optical micrographs were recorded by a bright-field microscope equipped with orthogonal polarizers (Nikon ECLIPSE Ti).

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: The reflection spectra were measured by a micro-angle-resolved spectrum system (Ideaoptics) equipped with a high-sensitive spectrometer (NOVA, Ideaoptics).

spans.heading: Characterizations
spans.text: The reflection optical photographs and videos were captured using a Canon EOS 7D camera and a smartphone under vertical incident white light.
